subject: Cost & residency: pricing bands and MAP (FinInsights)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Gretchen Wu <gretchen@fininsights.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost & residency follow-up (FinInsights pilot)

Hi Gretchen — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and two asks so we can lock the MAP next week.

Recap from our call:
- Use case: multi-tenant analytics assistant for financial research, PII redaction + audit logs retained 7 years per policy.
- Expected steady-state volume: 300–600M tokens / month (spiky during month-end reporting; peak +40%).
- Avg tokens per request: ~1.2k tokens (prompt + expected completion).
- Required data residency: EU primary (data must remain in EU with customer-controlled keys).
- Target procurement budget (initial pilot): $60k–$95k / month.
- Decision window: procurement + security by end of April; procurement prefers a 12–month committed price.

Two asks for pricing accuracy:
1) Confirm the monthly token range you expect to commit (low and high).
2) Tell us the target $/1M tokens band you need us to hit for the pilot to be approved (gives us the right discount profile to propose).

What I want to surface while you confirm numbers: EU-residency adds infra and compliance cost (regional GPUs, KMS/HSM, audit retention) — we typically see a 15–22% premium versus our US-hosted baseline. That premium varies with commit term and exact SLA (eg. longer retention or higher SLA increases cost).

I attached a short usage sample and a blank MAP template so we can populate mutual action items once numbers are confirmed.

Next steps: reply with the confirmed monthly range + target $/1M tokens and I’ll return a committed pricing table with banded discounts (no surprises, clear unit economics).

Thanks —
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments:
- MAP-FinInsights-v1.pdf (draft)
- usage-sample.csv
From: Gretchen Wu <gretchen@fininsights.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: FinInsights Sales Ops <salesops@fininsights.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Cost & residency follow-up (FinInsights pilot)

Hi Olga — thanks for the summary. Confirming the numbers we discussed:
- Expected committed volume for pilot: 350M tokens/month (target); high-case 550M/month.
- Target procurement budget for pilot: $70k–$90k / month.
- Target unit price we need to justify: ideally <= $260 / 1M tokens (EU residency is a hard requirement for data-at-rest).

A couple clarifying notes:
- We will need customer-controlled KMS and separate audit logs retained for 7 years.
- Procurement prefers a 12-month committed deal with quarterly usage true-ups.

If you can provide 1) what that $260 target maps to in committed-band pricing and 2) an example spend projection so we can show finance the NPV over 12 months, we’ll loop in security/procurement this week.

—Gretchen
Head of Product Operations, FinInsights
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Gretchen Wu <gretchen@fininsights.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost & residency follow-up (FinInsights pilot)

Gretchen — appreciate the clarity. Below is a concise pricing/units view and two committed options that map to your target band. I’ve tried to be explicit about where the EU-residency delta comes from so procurement can sign off faster.

Baseline assumptions (for transparency):
- Steady tokens: 350M/month (pilot target), peak 550M.
- Avg tokens per request: 1.2k.
- Baseline US-hosted unit (no residency): $240 / 1M tokens (this is our standard rack-rate before commit discounts).
- EU residency operational delta: +18% on unit cost (regional GPU capacity, customer KMS integration, and additional audit storage/ingest).

Option A — 12m committed (recommended for procurement predictability)
- Committed volume: 350M / month (12m).
- Unit price (US): $210 / 1M tokens (12m commit discount applied).
- Unit price (EU residency): $248 / 1M tokens (US unit * 1.18).
- Effective monthly spend (at committed 350M): US: ~$73,500; EU: ~$86,800.
- Notes: includes standard 99.9% uptime SLA; audit logs retention 7 years included; customer-managed KMS (key wrapping) add-on included.

Option B — Pilot flex (lower commit, allows growth)
- Committed volume: 200M / month initial with up to 12m conversion option.
- Unit price (US): $260 / 1M tokens.
- Unit price (EU residency): $307 / 1M tokens.
- Effective monthly spend (at 350M run rate, billed at blended rates): estimated ~$90k (blended).
- Notes: lower commit gives you headroom, higher unit price.

How this maps to your $260 target:
- Your target of <= $260 / 1M tokens (EU-residency constraint) is achievable under Option A (EU unit $248 / 1M). Option B would exceed that target at the EU unit price.

Unit economics breakdown (simple):
- Token unit = compute + storage/retention + ops premium for residency.
- At 350M tokens/month and EU unit price $248 => monthly cost estimate $86,800 => annual committed spend ~ $1.04M.
- If you require stricter SLA or >7y retention the EU premium would shift toward +22–25%.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm which option procurement prefers (A or B) and that the KMS + 7-year retention scope is acceptable.
2) If Option A, we’ll draft the MAP and run it through legal for a 12m SOW; estimated internal approvals 2 business days.
3) I’ll seed a DocuSign link and a populated MAP (attached updated MAP-FinInsights-v1.pdf).

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-minute call with our security lead to walk through KMS and audit retention details.

Thanks —
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- MAP-FinInsights-v1.pdf (updated)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost & residency follow-up (FinInsights pilot)

Quick internal — perfect alignment. Approve Option A pricing and the KMS + 7y retention scope. Approvals: Commercial approves the unit math; Legal ok to fast-track standard SOW with the MAP; Security will join the call if FinInsights requests deeper KMS details.

One ask before we send the DocuSign: add a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month-one committed spend (helps cover data ingest and SI work). That keeps us within procurement budget expectation while preserving unit economics.

I’ll let you send the updated MAP with that onboarding credit line item; I can be on the signature thread if needed.

—Rishi
Director, Sales — EMEA, Redwood Inference
